title: Looking, reaching, or crying when someone leaves
summary: Most babies react when you leave, by looking, reaching, or crying, by about 9 months, CDC says.
body: CDC's examples are a look, a reach, or tears. One of them is enough for the way the sentence is written. The line records a protest or a reach at parting. It is not a laboratory attachment category and not a score of the relationship. Most, here, means 75 percent or more of children, and the materials are not a screening test.

sources.title: Milestones by 9 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US government public domain. Supports 'Reacts when you leave (looks, reaches for you, or cries)'.
